summary: The session discusses the increasing pressure on data departments to deliver reliable data at scale amidst growing complexity and demands. It emphasizes the importance of a practical DataOps operating model and outlines ten best practices to maintain pipeline stability while fostering continuous innovation. The speaker highlights the need for operational excellence through a combination of disciplined practices and platform capabilities.

key_points: Organizations struggle to deliver fit-for-purpose data at scale.
The operating conditions have fundamentally changed, outgrowing past models.
Operational excellence is defined by reliable delivery, quality, and trust.
Data governance practices are essential for maintaining data integrity.
Foundation and planning involve forming cross-functional teams.
Execution and engineering focus on automation and orchestration.
Fusion teams enhance delivery reliability and velocity.
Prototyping and proof of value cycles help manage backlogs effectively.
Data contracts must be machine-readable and enforceable.
Observability is crucial for monitoring data quality and lineage.
Shift to self-service platforms improves accountability and reliability.
AI-assisted capabilities can enhance data delivery processes.
Fusion teams and standard data contracts are essential for success.
Automation and observability are not optional in modern DataOps.

key_takeaways: Implement fusion teams to enhance collaboration and delivery speed.
Establish standard data contracts to automate processes effectively.
Focus on automation and observability to ensure operational excellence.
